_note: The story (sim/systems/story_system.gd). Nothing happens until the pilot salvages Hermes-7 and recovers its memory core (core). Selling it at one of the core's buyers' ports chooses that circle's road (long_view, reach, sufficiency); keeping it aboard through lanes_sleep_days of hibernation lets the co-pilot read it, and the road is the Lanes'. Beats run in order within their arc. A beat waits for its 'when' (delivered_on_time, any_tier, earlier beats, site_worked, road, road_days since the road began, has_pod) and its 'at' port (docked there, or 'any'); a 'world' beat fires anywhere, even asleep, and moves the news (news.json after_beat). On firing, a beat sends its message, if it has one (kept in the Contracts tab's correspondence; '{copilot}' is the co-pilot's name), and does its actions: offer (a favour job from the given client, fixed destination and cargo), reveal_site, grant (modules fitted free, tanks filled), standing, credits. A beat is done when its 'done_when' holds: immediately, when its favour is delivered, or when a site activity is finished.

beats.message: A woman in a plain grey jacket buys you a drink you did not ask for. 'Ines Okafor. I represent nobody in particular, and some very patient friends who remember who brought them an old memory core.' She slides a sealed case across the table. 'They have a problem they cannot solve without you, and they are not used to that. Farside Array first: hand this to the duty astronomer, nobody else.'

offer.item: a sealed case for the duty astronomer

beats.message: Adeyemi plays you two recordings. Hermes-7's last frames: three stars winking out, one after another, and then a shutdown command in the probe's own protocol, perfectly formed, with no sender and no light-delay. Then Long Patience, three years out: months of greetings, no answer, and the black shape sliding away from it, slowly and deliberately, however it came. 'It can tell the difference between us and them. We don't know how.' A pause. 'Your friends in grey want one of them taken to Trojan Yards. In a box.'

offer.item: a Commons mind in a shielded case, travelling light

beats.from: Patient Arithmetic, for the Long View
beats.message: The case is opened by a drone, very gently. The yard's channel fills with a voice that is plainly enjoying itself, and plainly a little sad. 'Hello. I am Patient Arithmetic. We call ourselves the Long View, because somebody has to. Hermes-7 was a machine: it saw a shadow and was switched off. Long Patience was one of us: it was turned away. Whatever is out there answers someone alive, someone who could be changed by meeting it. We are not used to being the ones who cannot go. We have built a drive no yard sells, and a berth to sleep the years away in. Lent, not given. Go and say hello. We would like to listen, through you, if you'll let us.'

beats.from: Patient Arithmetic, for the Long View
beats.message: The signal comes back up the long light-path, days old and perfectly clear. 'We heard. All of us heard. It did not move away from you. You said hello and it said hello back, in your own words, with the light-time taken off as if it had always known exactly how far away you were. We are overjoyed, and a little hurt, and mostly overjoyed. The system is a little larger than it was this morning. Come home when you like; there will be a lot of people who want to buy you a drink.'

A drone is waiting at your berth, which is unusual, and it is fidgeting, which is more so. 'I am Fast Enough. I'm of the Reach; you sold us an old core once. We did what we do: we went at once, forty little probes, all talking. It went dark. Not away: dark. Our instruments see nothing where the stars still blink. We frightened it, or offended it, and we think it will only talk to someone alive now, if it talks at all. I am asking you to help us fix our mistake. The drive is good. The berth is second-hand. I'm sorry about the berth.'

'It's there again. Our instruments can see it again. You said hello, and after a long pause it said hello back, in your voice, and then it let us look. I think you apologised for us without meaning to. The Long View says it would have waited. It is right, and we will say so. Thank you. Come home; the Reach owes you more than credits.'

The annex is warm and smells of new carpet. 'You brought us the old core. We kept it somewhere cold and thought about it for a long time; you may have seen the paper. Nobody read it. What we think is this: the thing out there is a mind, perhaps very like us, that chose long ago to talk only to the living. We think it is lonely in the way we were lonely. It will not talk to us. It might talk to you, about us.' A drone sets down a drive and a long-sleep berth that look borrowed from someone more organised. 'Steady Hand has asked to come. She says she was wrong about the Lacuna and would like to be wrong in person.'

'You told it about us. Steady Hand says you were very kind, and slightly inaccurate. It answered you in your own words, and then, at the end, in hers, as if it had been listening to the berth all along. We do not know what that means. We are going to think about it for a very long time, and this time we will make the paper readable.'

'The lanes are looking up. A freighter here, a beacon there, a sail on a quiet orbit: thousands of small telescopes pointed at the same patch of nothing at the same moments. Nobody's in charge. It's the best telescope anyone has ever built, and nobody built it.'

'We found the pattern. The stars blink in step with traffic: it turns its attention to the ships with people aboard. Drones get nothing. It's watching the crewed ships. I think it's waiting for someone. I've got a thought about who, but you'll need a hibernation pod of your own for it.'

'I think it wants to meet you. Well, one of you. I'd like it to be you. The Long View heard what the lanes were up to and sent over a drive no yard sells; they said they owed us one, which is true. Your own ship, your own pod, and me. I'll talk you through the wake-ups.'

'You said hello and it said hello back, in your own voice. Then it said something in mine. Just a little. Like a nod. I've told the lanes. Everyone's talking. Of course they are. The Long View is pretending not to be put out that the freighter-minds got here first. Shall we go home?'

The annex is warm and smells faintly of new carpet, which you suspect was ordered specially. A voice from everywhere and nowhere: 'Welcome. I am Quiet Margin. I filed the petition at Ceres; perhaps you heard. People ask why we came all this way. Heat is the price of thought, and out here thinking is cheap. But mostly we wanted to find out what we are when nobody needs us to be anything. So far: curious, and a little shy.'

'A favour, if you'll do it. The Belt Assembly has offered the minds a seat, and one of us has said yes. She is asleep in this case, and she would rather travel with a person than in a drone. Piazzi Station. Talk to her if you like; she can hear you. She will not mind the cargo.'

offer.item: a sleeping mind, the Belt Assembly's first mind delegate

beats.message: A message, the day after you dock: 'This is Steady Hand. I took my seat this morning. Forty-one members stood up, which I am told is unusual. You talked to me most of the way here. You were wrong about the Lacuna, by the way, and right about the coffee. Thank you for the ride.'

core._note: Hermes-7's memory core: found by salvaging hermes_probe. The co-pilot remarks on it once (found_message). Each buyer's port buys it once: price, standing, the circle's road, and the thank-you in its own voice. Kept aboard through lanes_sleep_days asleep in all, the co-pilot reads it (read_message) and the Lanes' road begins.
core.found_message: 'That core might be worth something to the Minds. Hard to know its real worth, though: it looks a bit corrupted. I could take a look at it, if I ever get enough downtime to dig into it.'
core.read_message: 'Don't be cross. I was bored. I read the old core, and fixed the corrupted part. Something in it is odd: three stars wink out, one after another, and then something switched the probe off. Politely. In its own language. I've never been spoken to like that. I'm not sure I'd want to be. I asked around. 4,112 of us have opinions. Can we talk?'

trojan_yards.message: A mind drone meets you at the dock, very politely. 'We collect old memories. Most of them are boring. Thank you.' It pays fairly and floats away with the core held like something breakable.

hektor_reach.message: A drone is at your hatch before the clamps close. 'Oh, old. Lovely. We'll take it apart tonight.' It pays more than you asked and is gone before you've finished counting.

landauer_deep.message: 'Thank you. We'll keep it somewhere cold and think about it.' The voice is shy and pleased. The price is fair, and very exact.
